_comment: Every total, annular and hybrid solar eclipse and every total and partial lunar eclipse from 2026 to 2040. Dates, times of greatest eclipse and the visibility/track wording come from NASA/GSFC's decade tables (eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov, SEdecade + LEdecade); penumbral lunar eclipses are left out because almost nobody can tell one from an ordinary full Moon. total_boxes are coarse [lat_min, lat_max, lon_min, lon_max] boxes around the regions NASA lists in its [Total: ...] / [Annular: ...] bracket, and they are REGIONS, NOT THE TRACK: NASA names whole countries the path crosses, so a box around Australia covers Perth as well as the bit of the path near Sydney. Nothing here ever tells one place it will see totality -- inside a box we say the track is nearby and to check a detailed map, outside it we say partial. Under-claiming is the safe direction. 2029 has no total or annular solar eclipse at all, only partials, which is why the solar list skips it.
